## Existing seams and permitted additions

`PanelView(root,world)` owns command map, panel construction, storage choice and highlight. `GameView` owns latest state, actual active panel, root events, focus traps and lifecycle. Preserve `PanelKind`, UiActions and public GameView signatures.

Add **`PanelView.resetSession(): void`**, called by existing **`GameView.resetPresentation()`**. Reset local destination/source intent, expansion memory, command map and highlights/inline panel result when a New/import/Continue/replacement enters. Do not infer session identity from per-tick object identity, and do not reset on ordinary refresh, pause or panel switching. No persistent UI/save fields.

Panel-local expansion memory can use semantic group IDs; read native details state before rerender/switch and restore it without recreating hidden focus targets. An explicit panel-local select/control handler is allowed, routed through GameView's one delegated listener; no competing capture/focus listener. `data-command-key` remains based on the full semantic GameCommand, not label/order. After reordering retain focused eligible commands. If a one-time action becomes completed/hidden, focus a visible outcome/group summary or next useful control, never a hidden descendant; Return remains a safe fallback. Expand an explicitly focused finding/container group as needed before focusing its existing target.

Notice channels, active-time TTL, HUD priority and panel-versus-toast routing belong to2D and remain unchanged here. Keep the single existing `panel-feedback` API/element; its location/style may be made compact. Do not suppress errors by CSS or parse saved feedback into a new notice policy.2D will remove the existing action-feedback duplication once its wiring is reconciled.

## Player-facing result

### Hold

Use a compact header/navigation and one `Paused` status. Remove the repeated subtitle/intro, use `Hold` as its title, and put capacity/suit facts in a concise status row. The current top-screen power tutorial and repeated paragraphs must not push cargo or useful actions below the first viewport.

Order: carried items and their useful actions; accessible containers/bulk materials; nearby craft service/fitting; expandable Power; expandable Elsewhere. Use responsive compact rows/cards, not a wall of equally prominent paragraphs. Display what can actually be used here. Keep essential equipment/capacity visible and emergency meal accessible even when no meal is carried. Keep repeated meals/cells/buoy and transfer functionality; all existing material quantities remain transferable in the same increments. No hover-only help or tiny unlabeled icons.

Label cells as readable stable `Reserve cell N` by deterministic instance order, and modules from registry labels. If multiple containers make identity ambiguous, add the container name compactly. Never render raw `item_…` identifiers in ordinary panel text/labels. Underlying command/save IDs remain exact. Preserve installed-module capacity/socket/tradeoff information and actual refusal reasons. Supported charge/repair and fitting actions should be near the relevant craft, not in another top-screen manual. Disabled/occupied recovery retains all existing local-safe actions and limitations.

Power remains deliberately discoverable: pulse cost and next usable cell/charge, local recharge, reserve-hull use and no-charge quiet/cover/retreat options. Put full restrictions behind its accessible expansion; do not replace them with misleading success labels or hide the only route to needed actions. Elsewhere summarizes only existing known containers and their real status. Return/recovery information moves to Notebook and appears contextually in Hold for an active loss/cache/operation; do not discard a material recovery notice or make rescue actions inaccessible.

### Fabricate

Title `Fabricate`. Show a compact current/required bench line and useful recipes immediately. Readiness is **`craftingRefusal(state,id,world) === null`**, with one-time completion checked separately. Blueprint filtering stays. Group ready here first, then material shortage, prerequisite/site/space/clearance blocked work with actionable concise reason, then collapsed completed **one-time** references. Do not incorrectly label every non-ready recipe as only missing materials, or hide available repeated recipes after a prior craft. A reachable useful action must not disappear because another condition also fails.

Recipe costs use registry data; usable counts come from `available` and the actual `fabricationContainers` authority. Distinguish quantities not usable at this bench without double-counting usable carried stock, fitted/maintenance items or overlapping bins. Maintenance recipes show their actual protected stock separately. No alternate spending preview that can disagree with command execution. Name unfulfilled recipe dependencies via their registry labels. Readiness/refusal and final command remain authoritative even if materials alone appear sufficient.

Name the bench that actually serves each recipe. `localBenchSite` reports restored benches and is not by itself sufficient for pod/workshop repair recipes: show their real location/restoration state, and never imply that an unrestored locker is spendable. At the wrong site, give one concise useful direction to a **known** required bench. Do not invent unknown-site exact pins. Restore recipes remain easy to find. Output-space/blocked-cradle cases retain their specific refusal and atomicity.

Move power controls/module fitting to Hold and known habitats/unfinished berth context to Notebook. Sorting/tending already belongs to the aimed E verb; remove redundant generic sorting buttons from Fabricate while preserving that existing action and protected recovery guidance. Repeated generic site refusal on every row is unnecessary when the header/group names the constraint; specific exceptions still appear near their action. When usable work exists at960×600, its first recipe/action should be visible without scrolling. Do not achieve this by hiding the important header/status/navigation or reducing readable text sizes.

### Notebook

Keep finding cards exactly: source/provenance, Observed, Hypothesis, Regional lead, current question/interpretation and personal record voice. Remove the generic intro and redundant recovered-blueprint counter. Compact operational preparation into a Dive check with truthful suit/hull/food/cell information; a full-tank rating must be labelled as a rating, not current remaining air. Keep full useful safety/recovery preparation accessible in expandable content. Places are only discovered/visited sites, with concise actual capabilities. Known habitats remain linked to observed source context. The unfinished carrier berth remains clearly future construction in this milestone. No new lore, guidance unlock or early-spoiler copy.

### Storage intent

Track **explicit** choice separately from the current implicit default. An unchosen default updates contextually to an accessible local refuge locker, then deployed buoy, then craft hold. Thus Dart-only → walk to restored workshop defaults to its locker. A deliberately chosen accessible destination persists across refresh and temporary roster changes at the same meaningful service site; an accessible craft coming into/out of range must not erase that intent. Leaving that site or session replacement resets context; if the choice becomes inaccessible/identical to source, choose a valid fallback and give compact contextual feedback rather than silently promising the old destination.

Use a stable semantic site/anchor identity based on existing nearPod/nearWorkshop/local/support/access queries, not rounded coordinates or a joined accessible-container roster. A repaired/bench-versus-cradle transition alone is not grounds to lose an explicit choice for that same site. With no explicit choice, adding a newly accessible preferred locker may improve the default. Keep From valid and whole-set materialStoragePreview behavior exact. No auto-move.
